12.0.0.en: A great wonder: a marvelous scene and event.

12.0.1.en: A woman clothed with the sun: the Church wrapped in her Christ (the Sun of righteousness). The moon under her feet: the moon here may symbolize the bodies and relics of the saints and the stories of their labors, on which the Church stands, so that she increases in splendor and beauty.

12.0.2.en: Upon her head a crown: the crown always signifies kingship and authority ... and the twelve stars (that is, the Apostles, the pure disciples of Christ) are her authority, her preaching and the secret of her priesthood.

12.0.3.en: The meaning that the first verse carries as a whole is a radiant picture of the Church, which declares that the secret of her strength is her attachment to Christ, the true Light, borne up by faith, striving and the radiance of the virtues of her saints, and her authority is in the power of the sacrament of her priesthood, handed down from Christ to the pure Apostles by His pure, holy breathing. This woman also signifies the Virgin Mary and her Son Christ, as the Thursday praise in our Church mentions. She also signifies the soul that loves God, which Satan wars against and which brings forth many virtues in Christ.

12.1.0.en: She cried, travailing in birth: the severe pains of childbirth.

12.1.1.en: From her first days the Church is a mature mother able to give birth, and her pains point to her constant striving to bring forth "God the Word" in the hearts of her children, or in other words to bring forth children strong in the faith.

12.2.1.en: A great red dragon: a reference to Satan in his evil, his severity and his bloodthirstiness.

12.2.2.en: Seven heads: a reference to the power of his thoughts, and their multiplicity and variety.

12.2.3.en: Ten horns: the horn in an animal represents its strength in attack, and ten horns means that he uses all his strength and energies.

12.2.4.en: Seven crowns upon his heads: that is, he has authority over his children and his soldiers and those who follow him in the whole world.

12.3.1.en: In some creatures the tail is considered the strongest thing in them (like the crocodile or the scorpion), and the verse here is a continuation of the explanation of Satan's strength, describing his tail with the strength by which he was able to bring down the angels who followed him at his fall. The mention of the number of a third is a reference to his strength on the one hand, but also that those he was able to bring down are a limited number, since two thirds remained.

12.3.2.en: Stood before the woman: he announces his challenge to the Church.

12.3.3.en: To devour her child: the child here is a direct reference to the Lord Christ Himself, whom the Church wants to bring forth in her children, and Satan lies in wait for His birth in order to kill the work of the Church in preaching Christ.

12.4.0.en: The meaning here is clear and direct and admits only the person of Christ Himself, whom Satan wanted to swallow by death, but He swallowed death. He is the One of whom David prophesied, "I will give thee the heathen for thine inheritance ... Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron" (Ps 2:9). To rule all nations: that is, He accepts everyone from every place so long as they believe in Him and in His commandments.

12.4.1.en: A rod of iron: it shows the strength of His authority over His enemies.

12.4.2.en: Caught up unto God, and to his throne: a reference to His Resurrection, His Ascension and His sitting at the right hand of the Father.

12.5.0.en: The woman fled: that is, she went far away and escaped the harm of Satan.

12.5.1.en: The Church finds her rest in the wilderness, away from the world of sin, where her God sustains her completely, as He sustained Elijah and sustained His people for the forty years in the wilderness of Sinai. The wilderness also points to austerity and renunciation of the world and its pleasures. As long as a person is detached and limited in his needs, he can nullify the wars of Satan, since material things lose their authority over him.

12.5.2.en: A place prepared: that is, God, by His foreknowledge, prepared for her everything she needs throughout the time of her sojourn away from the world. A thousand two hundred ...: it signifies the short time that is followed by eternity (see ch. 11:3).

12.5.3.en: My beloved God ... the love of the world often hinders us and keeps us from setting out to You and enjoying You. Blessed are the fathers of the wilderness, who left everything for Your sake ...; grant us also to leave what occupies us away from You, that we too may win Your companionship.

12.6.s.en: (2) The casting out of Satan from heaven

12.6.0.en: Many of the Fathers saw that this whole scene, that is, these three verses, speaks of things that happened before the creation of man, and therefore this war is a war waged by the archangel Michael against Satan and all his followers whom he led astray, and Michael was able to cast them all out, because it is not reasonable for Satan to remain after his fall standing before God among His luminous creation. Those who hold this opinion prove it by what came in the Book of Job when God asked Satan, "Whence comest thou?" and Satan answered, "From going to and fro in the earth" (Job 1:7). The meaning of this is that Satan's authority became confined to the earth after his fall and expulsion.

12.6.1.en: As for the other opinion in interpretation, it avoids fixing the time of this scene and considers that what John saw here represents heaven's support of the Church in her war against Satan in the time of her sojourn, so that Satan's power is greatly diminished. This expression is very consoling to the Church, for despite the power of the dragon, he is weaker than the archangel Michael and his angels.

12.6.2.en: The great dragon: an expression indicating the strength of Satan.

12.6.3.en: That old serpent: this is also his title after he took the form of the serpent when he seduced Adam and Eve. Satan: the best-known of his names, and it is Hebrew, meaning "the adversary or the opponent." The Devil: his Greek name, meaning "the accuser."

12.6.4.en: Which deceiveth the whole world: by his deception and people's believing him, since he is "a liar, and the father of it" (Jn 8:44). Cast out into the earth: a reference to the fact that his power is limited before the archangel Michael, who defeated him and cast him out.

12.6.5.en: God in His love supports us in our striving by the intercessions of the angels on our behalf and their help to us in all our works. Would that we make use of this love and establish friendship with them, so that we are strengthened and advance with confidence in our spiritual life.

12.7.0.en: I heard a loud voice: a new proclamation in a raised voice, made by one of the angels.

12.7.1.en: Now is come salvation of our God: that is, the salvation of all who believe in His name, and salvation is ascribed to God because it is He who offered it to mankind.

12.7.2.en: The accuser is cast down: that is, Satan is cast out (v. 9). Accused them: that is, Satan's work is accusing, envying the children of God and fighting them, as in (Job 1:11). Day and night: a figure for Satan's perseverance and diligence in ensnaring the children of God. With the fall of Satan from heaven and his confinement to the earth, the heavenly creation proclaimed its glorification of God the Father and His Christ, that is, His only-begotten Son, and this glorification consists of thanking God for His victory and His plan of salvation through His Son the Redeemer, and the proclamation of His sole and everlasting reign and authority.

12.8.0.en: They overcame him: that is, the victory was accomplished for the children of God.

12.8.1.en: By the blood of the Lamb: that is, the blood of Christ shed on the wood of the Cross and offered to the world for salvation.

12.8.2.en: By the word of their testimony: that is, the faith that they accepted and preached, and suffered for, and perhaps were martyred for. This verse presents the secret of the victory of the believing children of God. They took refuge in the blood of Christ poured out for them, through their faith in the power and effectiveness of this blood for salvation and through the sacrament of the Eucharist, in which Christ gives us His precious and most holy Blood. Their lives also became a witness to Christ in all their conduct and in bearing the pains of persecution, whatever they were. St. John gives us the reason for their endurance and steadfastness, which is that they loved their God Christ more than their lives, so they cared nothing for what happened to them, even if it was death itself.

12.9.0.en: Therefore: that is, because of the proclamation of salvation and the authority of Christ (v. 10) and because of the victory of the children of God (v. 11).

12.9.1.en: The invitation to joy and jubilation was addressed to the heavenly creation with all that is in it, because of the preceding events: the casting down of Satan to the earth and his confinement, the proclamation of the victory and authority of Christ, and likewise the victory of all His children through their acceptance of faith in the effectiveness of His blood for salvation.

12.9.2.en: Woe to the inhabiters of the earth: that is, a warning to all the inhabitants of the earth of the severity of what is to come ...

12.9.3.en: Since Satan knew that he has a short time before the Second Coming of Christ and the proclamation of the general judgment, the wrath of his failure became great, like a wounded animal, and for this reason he is about to pour out his wrath on the Church in various and severe wars.

12.10.s.en: (3) The war on the earthly Church

12.10.0.en: Exactly what was warned of in the previous verse (v. 12) took place, but God by His grace gave the Church two wings with which she can rise above all the wars of Satan: "They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles" (Isa 40:31). These two wings are the subject of the meditations of many of the Fathers, and among them are those who saw:

12.10.1.en: a) That they are the two Testaments (Old and New), by which a person rises to the lofty heavens of contemplation. b) Or that they are faith and works, which are the two wings of salvation and of reaching the Kingdom. c) Or that they are the greatest commandments, of loving God with all the heart and a person's loving his fellow man. d) Some also saw that they are the pure wings of prayer and fasting, by which the worship of God is made upright. Fly into the wilderness, where she is nourished: see (v. 6). For a time, and times, and half a time: as in (v. 6) also, with a difference in expression, for the word time means a year, so the meaning is (a year + two years + half a year), that is, three and a half years or one thousand two hundred and sixty days ... This time has been repeated often and always means a limited period, since it is half of the number seven, which indicates perfection ... The meaning intended as a whole is that the Church will be kept in the wilderness that God prepared for her throughout the time of her persecution, which is relatively short compared with the times of glory in eternity.

12.11.0.en: In a new war to drown the Church in the world, Satan cast out of his mouth much water "as a flood." These waters point to the many wicked multitudes of the world who want to carry the Church away from the wilderness, the place of her sustenance and her God's care, and draw her into the world and its lusts, for Satan knows perfectly well that if the Church leaves her wilderness (v. 6) she loses all her strength.

12.12.0.en: The earth helped the woman: that is, God by His power made some of the inhabitants of the earth stand before Satan and defend His Church.

12.12.1.en: Some saw that this river (v. 15) is the river of Jewish and Roman persecution, and the help that came from the earth was the stopping of this persecution by the decree of the Emperor Constantine and the recognition of Christianity as one of the religions acknowledged in the ancient Roman state.

12.12.2.en: The general spiritual meaning is that the Church is kept in God's plan throughout the time of her sojourn on earth, and God by His power is able to raise up from among her opponents defenders of her, so that He scatters all the wars of the evil Satan.

12.13.0.en: Satan's rage at the failure of his attempts continued, but this anger did not dissuade him from continuing the war with the children of God and the Church, especially those who hold fast to keeping the commandments of Christ and acting on them.

12.13.1.en: I thank You, my Lord Jesus Christ, for You have revealed to us the secret of the Church's victory and gave us victory with her. Our strength is in Your sustaining and Your spiritual food offered to us in the wilderness, which, if the Church leaves it, she loses everything with it, and when she holds fast to it she nullifies all the wars of the evil enemy and triumphs over him. I thank You for these verses that encourage the soul in its striving throughout the time of its sojourn.

12.13.2.en: The two beasts, a general introduction: this chapter speaks of two beasts who are followers of the great dragon mentioned in (ch. 12), and who form with him a trinity whose whole aim is the destruction and deception of people. Since the dragon's first war was in heaven, the two beasts, his followers, one (came out of the sea) and the other (out of the earth), as a figure for the severity of Satan's war and its comprehensiveness!!...

13.0.s.en: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

13.0.0.en: I stood upon the sand of the sea: a preface to the fact that what he is about to see comes from the sea. The sand points to instability and lack of steadfastness, the sea to turbulence, and its waves to the multitudes of the wicked.

13.0.1.en: I saw a beast: a creature came out of the sea, and he described it as a beast because of its great evil.

13.0.2.en: Having seven heads and ten horns: see the explanation of the dragon in the previous chapter (v. 3). What draws our attention is the identity of the form of this beast with the dragon, and this means the identity of their aims, intentions and also their ferocity.

13.0.3.en: Some interpreters see that the seven heads and ten horns are seven nations and ten successive kings who support Satan and extend his authority, and they prove this by the crowns upon his heads, which only kings wear. Some of them explained that the ten horns and their crowns are the ten Roman emperors in their war on the Church, beginning with Nero and ending with Diocletian, which is the worst period of persecution the whole Church has witnessed. Upon his heads the name of blasphemy: whoever this beast is, his aim, which God reveals to us, is to blaspheme the name of God the Most High in order to lead people astray.

13.1.0.en: Like unto a leopard: in the swiftness of its pouncing, its ferocity and its treachery, for the leopard is an animal that preys on anything even if it is not hungry.

13.1.1.en: His feet were as the feet of a bear: the bear is a huge, heavy animal that sometimes walks on four and sometimes stands on its hind legs (its feet) ... The meaning is that the beast is like the bear when it displays its strength, standing and resting on its two strong legs.

13.1.2.en: His mouth as the mouth of a lion: that is, with the strength of its jaw when it closes upon prey.

13.1.3.en: And the dragon gave him: that is, the chief of the demons gave this beast, or these kingdoms, all his power and authority in the war against the Church and the children of God.

13.2.0.en: I saw one of his heads: that is, one of the seven heads.

13.2.1.en: As it were wounded: that is, it was not slain but plays a part in order to lead people astray, pretending weakness for a purpose of its own that we shall come to know.

13.2.2.en: His deadly wound was healed: that is, what the world supposed of death in him was not real, for he rose again with a power that astonished all the inhabitants of the earth, so that they offered Satan and his followers prostration and worship and the confession that they are the true power that cannot be overcome.

13.2.3.en: The spiritual meaning of these two verses is that Satan may pretend weakness for a short time in order to deceive the children of God, that perhaps they may become negligent in their striving, then he rises with force again, trying to devour them, and displays his strength so as to make the world follow him all the more and increase in its error and its denial of the power of God.

13.2.4.en: Beware, beloved, for there is no truce with the enemy in your striving and the days of your sojourn, and do not be amazed by the signs or miracles that Satan may bring in order to lead you astray, even if he imitates Christ in His death and resurrection, for he has no purpose but your destruction.

13.3.0.en: There was given unto him a mouth: that is, his power is not from himself, but God permitted him to use this power that Satan gave him.

13.3.1.en: Great things and blasphemies: that is, everything that attracts people on the one hand and everything that makes them doubt God on the other.

13.3.2.en: Power was given unto him: everything is by God's permission.

13.3.3.en: Forty and two months: that is, three and a half years, which is the time of the Church's sojourn in the wilderness (ch. 12:6), yet this period is a set period, just as the authority of Satan, however severe, is also limited.

13.3.4.en: Satan gave the beast of the sea power to blaspheme against God, and God permitted that for a limited time, which is 42 months.

13.4.0.en: He opened his mouth in blasphemy against God: he blasphemes the name of God, that is, he directs insults at the name of God, or it also means that he takes titles of God and ascribes them to himself.

13.4.1.en: His tabernacle: that is, he mocks the Church and makes the world scoff at her.

13.4.2.en: Them that dwell in heaven: he makes people doubt eternity and the other life with ideas of atheism and rational doubt.

13.4.3.en: The general meaning is that he fights without rest on all fronts: he attacks the name of God and transgresses against it, and attacks also His Church and the children of God who dwell with Him, and also mocks heaven and eternal life. My beloved brother: is this not what is happening now around us in the world, of Satan's success in attacking God and His Church in what they call the civilized world? The world in many places now claims that God is merely a myth in people's minds, and many European countries now proudly declare that they are secular states that have no connection with religion or Christianity ... Would that we learn to pray for the salvation of the world and the overthrow of the power of the evil Satan.

13.5.0.en: God also permitted the beast to make war with the children of God, that is, the saints.

13.5.1.en: To overcome them: that is, to kill whoever does not worship him. It is an apparent victory, but this takes nothing from their salvation and their heavenly inheritance.

13.5.2.en: Over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations: that is, the spread of his error, his blasphemy and his war in the whole world.

13.6.0.en: Part of the power of this beast is that everyone will submit to him, worship him and bow down to him, except the children of God. Whose names are written: that is, the children of God who are known to Him, whose names He kept in the book of life by His foreknowledge and knowledge of their striving, their holding fast to faith in Him and their resistance to Satan. This book of life, that is, eternal salvation, is ascribed to the slain Lamb, because there is no salvation or eternity outside faith in the blood of Christ.

13.6.1.en: Part of the power of this beast is that many who are condemned to eternal death will worship him, that is, those who did not believe and enjoy the salvation of Christ and were not written in the book of life.

13.7.0.en: If any man have an ear, let him hear: a warning of the importance of what has been said and a drawing of attention to what is coming.

13.8.0.en: This verse represents the end of the talk about the first beast with all his power, and the speech here is about God's final recompense to this beast and his kingdoms. Its general meaning is that treatment and judgment are in kind ... so everything the beast brought will turn back upon him.

13.8.1.en: Goeth into captivity: that is, as he took many captive and imprisoned them, his end will be prison and chains in the abyss.

13.8.2.en: Must be killed with the sword: God's justice and retribution are necessary in the end, because the end of this beast is destruction.

13.9.0.en: The speech here is about the second beast and the third enemy and what distinguishes him from the dragon and the first beast: Coming up out of the earth: the earth here symbolizes lowness and degradation, which is fitting for the description of the one who rises out of it.

13.9.1.en: He had two horns like a lamb: that is, he pretends the meekness of lambs, so that his speech is soft, gentle and attractive.

13.9.2.en: He spake as a dragon: that is, when he opened his mouth and his real thoughts appeared ... everyone became sure of his cruelty and that he is a beast like his predecessor, wanting nothing but the destruction of all.

13.9.3.en: All the interpreters agreed that this beast is the false prophet who comes in the time of lambs, as the Lord Christ warned His disciples (Mt 7:15). He "spake," that is, he used logic and lying in leading people astray, yet anyone who has spiritual discernment and sound faith can easily uncover his error.

13.10.0.en: He exercised all the power of the first beast: that is, he has the same power as the first beast in harming and preying.

13.10.1.en: Before him: he devotes all his efforts to the service of the first beast, that is, the Antichrist.

13.10.2.en: By the authority, power and ability to deceive that he has, this beast was able to make the multitudes of mankind bow down to and worship the first beast. The meaning we can draw is that the kingdom of evil with all its demons works in coordination and helps one another, for it is one dark kingdom and its one aim is to turn people away from God and destroy them.

13.11.0.en: He doeth great wonders: by his magic and his authority he brings what people believe to be extraordinary miracles, so that he imitated what Elijah did when he brought down fire from heaven (1 Kgs 18), with the difference of course that Elijah proclaimed the power of God, while the beast leads people astray. The purpose of all these works is dazzling and frightening, so that people submit to this liar and believe him, and then comes the second step, for which this beast appeared, which is to lead people, indeed to command and compel them, to worship the Antichrist, that is, the first beast. That they should make an image to the beast: that is, replacing the worship of God with the worship of Satan, or wiping the image of God from people's minds, so that nothing remains in their minds but the image of the Antichrist.

13.11.1.en: Who had the wound by a sword, and did live: the first beast, that is, the Antichrist (v. 3). The beast coming up out of the earth performs miracles such as bringing fire down from heaven to dazzle people and frighten them so that they worship the beast of the sea.

13.12.0.en: This evil one (the beast of the earth) was able to lead people astray and persuade them of the power of the first beast (the Antichrist) and that he is the true God, and he made an image or form for him, or perhaps by the power of magic he made his image speak and talk. So people believed in him, and everyone who refused and held fast to the sound faith was killed in a great persecution.

13.13.0.en: As God sealed His faithful servants with the Holy Spirit, that is, with the anointing of the Holy Myron, so also the beast did with his followers of all races, ages and classes, and this mark was: a) On their right hand: that is, he took possession of their will, for the hand represents the will.

13.13.1.en: b) In their foreheads: that is, he also controlled their minds and thoughts.

13.13.2.en: It can also be said that by his possessing a person's hand, he cannot raise his hand to make the sign of the Cross on his forehead so as to free his head from the thoughts of Satan and his authority.

13.14.0.en: Because of Satan's control over people, it became hard for those who refuse his mark, that is, the children of God, to live their lives and obtain their necessities, because the wicked refuse to deal with them. The name or mark of the beast: the sign that distinguishes his followers.

13.14.1.en: The number of his name: it will be explained in the next verse.

13.15.0.en: Here is wisdom: that is, knowing the identity of the beast and not being deceived by him and by all that he brings requires great wisdom, whose source is God and which is given only to the faithful who have held fast to the sound faith. The number of the beast .. the number of a man .. Six hundred threescore and six: this number (666) has wearied all the interpreters (to no avail) in their attempt to reach the name of the beast. They attributed the number to the Hebrew letters at one time and the Greek at another, and all of them came out with different conclusions that explained nothing, because the name is in the first place hidden from men, otherwise God would have declared it to them. After reviewing all the opinions of the early Fathers in their interpretation, honesty requires us to take the spiritual interpretation without entering into what we do not know. The number 6 is an incomplete number compared with the number 7, which indicates perfection, or the number 8, which indicates eternity. Accordingly we can say that God wants to reassure us that the first and second beast, and before them the dragon, with all they were able to do and bring, are incomplete and deficient before the divine perfection, and none of them brought anything except by God's permission and wisdom.

13.15.1.en: God wanted to reveal to us the nature of Satan, so he appeared to us as a dragon or a cruel and deceptive beast ... and we have no escape except taking refuge in the name of God, by calling upon Him and communing with Him, "for the name of the Lord is a strong tower" (Prov 18:10), and by continuing in union with Him through partaking of the Holy Mysteries, so that through Him we have victory over the beast and all his kingdom.

13.15.2.en: The Lamb and the believers ... and the harvest of the earth, a general introduction: the two preceding chapters showed Satan's resistance to the Church and the children of God with all his power through the dragon and the two beasts, in every place (heaven, sea and earth ...). Here we move to a comforting scene that proclaims the victory of the Lamb and the justice of God, which increases our hope in the time of our difficulties ...
